name: sigora Area Map
author: sigorauk

sections.description:
Buyers want to know about the area before they book a viewing. The sigora Area Map answers on your own listing pages: schools, transport, health, sold prices, crime, broadband and more around a live map of the home, every figure from an official UK source and set in your brand colours. It is made for estate and lettings agents in England.

  • Property Hive: install the plugin and the Area Map adds itself to every property page. It reads each home’s location from Property Hive’s own fields, with no template edits. The Area Map for Property Hive.
  • Any WordPress theme: add the sigora shortcode to your single-listing template once, with each listing’s postcode, plus its coordinates if you have them, and every listing shows its own area. The sigora block adds it to any single page in a couple of clicks. The Area Map for WordPress.

Start a free 30-day trial, no card needed: see the plans

Nine lenses. You choose which ones show.

  • Map: the whole area at a glance, on one map around the home.
  • Schools: the nearest schools, with their results and the sigora inspection summary.
  • Transport: the nearest stations and their lines, and every bus stop within a mile.
  • Health: GPs, pharmacies and dentists nearby, with inspection ratings and patient survey scores.
  • Prices: HM Land Registry sold prices near the home, set against the council area and England, with five-year trends.
  • Crime: the sigora crime rating, with Police.uk figures set against the council area and England.
  • Amenities: the cafés, restaurants, pubs, shops and everyday places within a walk.
  • Environment: air quality, noise, modelled long-term flood risk from rivers, sea and surface water where covered, and green space.
  • Connectivity: Ofcom broadband and mobile coverage, with address-level broadband speed where Ofcom has a match.

Set it up your way, once

Every lens can be switched on or off for your website in the sigora console, and the choice applies to every listing. Lead with Schools if families are your buyers; leave Crime off if it will not help.

  • Smart rules: show Crime only where it is better than the national average, and show air quality only when it is acceptable.
  • Want a big map? Keep the area summary collapsed for a full-width map.
  • Your look: your brand colour and a light or dark theme in the console; Standard or Tall height and a maximum width on the plugin’s sigora page, because your page needs those before the Area Map loads.

Area Reports included

Every plan includes Area Reports: branded, print-ready A4 reports for any address, not just your listings. Generate one from your console in seconds, with your logo on the cover and the same official evidence inside. Leave it with a vendor after a valuation or add it to the viewing pack.

Paid plans include 1,000 Area Reports a month and the free trial includes 15. There is no per-report charge. See a sample report (PDF).

Why agents trust it

  • Every figure names its source: ONS, DfE, HM Land Registry, Police.uk, NHS, Ofcom and more.
  • No cookies, no visitor tracking: the Area Map adds nothing your visitors need to consent to.
  • One install covers every listing: no per-property work, ever.
  • Free for 30 days: full access, no card needed.
  • Simple plans: from £19.99 a month per website, sized by how many listings you have live, with every lens and Area Reports on every plan. See plans.

More about the Area Map.

sigora is an independent product. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Property Hive. Property Hive compatibility means the plugin detects Property Hive and places the Area Map on its property pages.

External services

This plugin relies on sigora, a hosted third-party service, to render the
Area Map and supply its data. The plugin does not bundle the Area Map’s
runtime and cannot show anything without it.

What is sent, where, and when:

  1. Hosted script. On every page where the Area Map is placed, the visitor’s
    browser loads the sigora script from
    https://sigora.uk/widgets/v1/sigora-widget.js, the address your sigora
    account returns during a connection test. As with any externally hosted
    script, that request sends the visitor’s IP address, user agent, and the page
    URL as referrer.

  2. Local-area data. The loaded script then requests area data from the sigora
    API at https://sigora.uk. It sends your public sigora site key, your site’s
    origin, the page URL, and the listing context you configured for that
    placement – latitude and longitude, or postcode, or place slug – together with
    the listing reference. It does not send names, email addresses, or any other
    personal data held by WordPress.

  3. Connection test. When an administrator presses Test connection on the
    plugin’s sigora page, WordPress makes one server-side request to
    https://sigora.uk/api/v1/public/widget/plugin/diagnostic carrying your site
    key and your site’s origin. Nothing is sent at any other time.

  4. Optional listing inventory. Only if you save a private inventory token,
    sigora reads your published Property Hive listing records from this site over
    an authenticated REST route on its own schedule. Remove the saved token to
    revoke that access. The token is never emitted in page HTML or in public REST
    output.

The service is provided by Sigora Insights Ltd (https://sigora.uk). Using this
plugin means accepting that provider’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Terms of service: https://sigora.uk/legal/b2b-tos
  • Privacy policy: https://sigora.uk/privacy
  • Data processing addendum: https://sigora.uk/legal/b2b-dpa
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins, Add New and search for sigora, then Install
    Now. Or upload the sigora-widget folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or
    install the ZIP from the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate “sigora Area Map”.
  3. Open sigora in the WordPress left-hand menu.
  4. Paste the site key from your sigora console. If you do not have one, use
    the Start free trial link.
  5. Run Test connection to check the site key, WordPress origin, plan state,
    and script address. It should say Ready.
  6. If Property Hive is active, leave automatic placement on for property
    pages. Otherwise, add the sigora block or shortcode where the Area Map
    should appear.

On a Property Hive property page, a bare [sigora_widget] uses that property’s
own location. Anywhere else, give it the listing’s location, for example
(wire the postcode to the listing’s own postcode field):

[sigora_widget postcode="..." listing_id="..."]

Where listings carry coordinates, add lat/lng as well; the postcode stays,
because Connectivity (broadband and mobile signal) needs it
([sigora_widget postcode="..." listing_id="..." lat="..." lng="..."]).
On a Property Hive property page, a shortcode that gives coordinates still
picks up the property’s postcode and reference when it leaves them out.
Lenses, layout, colours and theme come from your sigora console, so they are
not set in the shortcode.
sections.faq:
Do I need Property Hive?

No. The sigora block and shortcode work on any WordPress site. If you do use
Property Hive, the Area Map adds itself to your property pages and reads each
listing’s location, so there is nothing to place by hand.

Can I choose which lenses appear?

Yes. Switch any of the nine lenses on or off for your website in the sigora
console. The smart rules for Crime and air quality are set there too.

Are Area Reports included?

Yes. Every paid plan includes 1,000 co-branded Area Reports a month, and the
free trial includes 15. There is no per-report charge.

What versions are supported?

The compatibility floor is WordPress 6.0+, PHP 7.4+, and Property Hive 1.5+ when
Property Hive mode is active. The admin Plugin health view reports the installed
WordPress, PHP, and Property Hive versions.

How does the plugin authenticate with sigora?

The plugin uses the public sigora site key and the detected WordPress site
origin. There is no plugin API key and no separate identity stack.

What does Test connection check?

Test connection calls the sigora plugin diagnostic endpoint with the configured
site key and detected site origin. It reports missing site key, invalid key,
blocked origin, inactive site, plan-derived lens availability, and bundle URL
state when the sigora backend returns those fields.

Why is the Area Map not showing on a Property Hive listing?

Automatic placement uses Property Hive’s standard property page: it adds the
Area Map after the property details, or after the description where a theme
prints it through WordPress’s normal content output. Some custom themes build
their own property page and skip both. If so, ask whoever built your website
to add [sigora_widget] to your property page template where the Area Map
should appear. On a Property Hive property page it needs nothing else: it uses
that property’s own location. The diagnostic log also records missing-location
and disabled-listing states for administrators.

Can I choose where the Area Map appears on my property pages?

Yes. Automatic placement uses one fixed spot. For a different spot, untick
automatic placement, add [sigora_widget] (or the sigora block) to your
property page template where you want it, and tick Custom property template so
your listings are still counted. A page never shows two Area Maps.

What location fields does Property Hive mode use?

sigora uses the property’s map pin from Property Hive (_latitude and
_longitude) first, then the older _property_location_latitude and
_property_location_longitude fields, then RealEstateListing JSON-LD
geo.latitude and geo.longitude. A 0,0 pin counts as not set. It also
keeps a postcode from common Property Hive postcode meta fields when coordinates
exist, because broadband and mobile evidence is postcode-keyed. A postcode is
the fallback location only when no usable coordinates are available.

Where do I set the lenses, layout, colours and size?

In your sigora console, the single place to configure how the Area Map looks.
The plugin only needs your site key; it does not duplicate those settings, so
nothing in WordPress can clash with your console. A single listing can still
narrow the lenses with the _sigora_show custom field (it cannot unlock lenses
that are not enabled for the site), and _sigora_disable skips placement for
that listing.

How does the plugin get updates?

Through WordPress, from the WordPress.org plugin directory. The plugin contains
no updater of its own and does not check any sigora URL for new versions, so
update checks, the update notice and the auto-updates toggle all behave exactly
as they do for any other directory plugin. Builds installed from a direct ZIP
before the directory listing existed are replaced by installing the directory
version once, after which updates arrive automatically.

Automatic updates stay off until you turn them on. Click “Keep sigora up to date
automatically” on the plugin’s sigora page, or use “Enable auto-updates” on the
Plugins screen; both change the same WordPress setting. Most improvements need
no plugin update at all, because the Area Map itself is served by sigora.

What data leaves my site?

See the External services section above. In short: visitors’ browsers load the
Area Map from sigora and sigora returns local-area data for the listing
location you configured. Nothing personal held by WordPress is sent.

Does the plugin track visitors?

No. The plugin renders the hosted Area Map, which sets no cookies and loads no
analytics scripts. Its events are aggregate runtime events tied to site and
listing context, not visitor identity.
sections.changelog:
0.2.11

  • Updated listing details.

0.2.10

  • Add private manifest-v2 PropertyHive listing attributes for opt-in backend ingestion. No assistant UI or account changes.

0.2.9

  • Clearer settings and shortcode examples.

0.2.8

  • Clearer shortcode guidance; Property Hive pages fill in each property’s postcode and reference.

0.2.7

  • Optional one-click automatic updates.

0.2.6

  • Improved phone layout and accessibility; updated screenshots.

0.2.5

  • Connect Property Hive listing inventory automatically after Test connection on HTTPS sites.
  • Keep manual inventory credentials behind Advanced.

0.2.4

  • Clearer setup guidance.
  • Minor improvements.

0.2.3

  • Improved Property Hive location handling.
  • More flexible placement for custom property templates.
  • Simpler settings page.
  • Minor improvements.

0.2.2

  • Add Widget height (Standard 520px / Tall 640px) and Maximum width to the Sigora admin page. PropertyHive automatic placement uses them; a shortcode or block height attribute still overrides the height.

0.2.1

  • Rename the plugin from “Sigora Widget for WordPress” to “Sigora Widget”. The WordPress.org plugin directory does not permit “WordPress” in a plugin name. The folder, main file, text domain, settings and site key are unchanged.
  • Document the Sigora external service in the readme: what is sent, when, and the provider’s terms, privacy policy and data processing addendum.
  • Accept health in per-listing lens overrides, so all nine lenses can be named in _sigora_show and in the block’s lens field.
  • List the nine lenses in the readme and replace the placeholder screenshots with real captures.

0.2.0

  • Add a private, paginated Property Hive listing inventory that Sigora can synchronize without visitor traffic.
  • Source publication and enablement remain separate from independent page verification.

0.1.0

  • Adds the top-level Sigora admin page with site-key storage, Property Hive
    auto-inject toggle, widget height, diagnostic log, partner links, and Test
    connection (lenses, layout, colours and theme are set in the Sigora console).
  • Adds generic shortcode and dynamic Gutenberg block rendering.
  • Adds Property Hive detection, automatic property-page injection, coordinate
    extraction, listing ID fallback, _sigora_show, and _sigora_disable.
  • Adds WordPress.org readme/assets, direct-download ZIP packaging, version
    compatibility matrix, GPL notice, and Plugin health diagnostics.

short_description: A live local area map on every property listing, from official UK data. Automatic on Property Hive, a shortcode on any theme. Area Reports included.

screenshots.caption: The area around the home on one full-width map: schools, stations, bus stops, GPs, pharmacies and green space within a mile, with the area summary a tap away.
Schools: the closest schools within a mile, each with its results and the sigora inspection summary.
Transport, for a home in Camden: seven Tube stations within a mile, each with its lines, plus the closest bus stop and every stop on the map.
Health, for a home in Hackney: the three nearest GP practices, each rated Good with CQC and patient-survey results, plus the nearest pharmacies and dentists.
Prices: HM Land Registry sold prices within a mile, set against the council area and England, with five-year trends by property type.
Crime: a clear sigora crime rating of Lowest, with the rate near the home well below Cheshire East and England.
Amenities, for a home in Camden: 1.8k everyday places within a mile, from 579 restaurants and cafés to parks, pubs and food shops, with the closest essentials.

Environment in Congleton: both Environment Agency long-term flood ratings, for rivers and the sea and for surface water, with the flood map, plus very clean air, road, rail and aircraft noise, and plentiful green space nearby.
Connectivity: gigabit broadband with a predicted 1,800 Mbps at this address, and strong mobile signal on all four networks.
Prefer the numbers beside the map? Set the area summary to open expanded and the nearest station, schools, GP, broadband and green space sit alongside it.
Area Reports included: co-branded, print-ready A4 pages for any address, with your logo on the cover.

You are in control: choose your brand colour, text colour, font and any map colour, switch each of the nine lenses on or off, pick a simpler school list or area summary, choose a map or data layout for Environment, and set smart rules for Crime and air quality; height and width are set where you install.
Made for phones too: the map first, then the area summary as a single, easy-to-scroll column.

Simple set-up in WordPress: paste your site key, pick Standard or Tall and a maximum width, and Property Hive sites switch on automatic placement with one tick. One click keeps the plugin up to date automatically.
